situation:
You are the client communications manager for QUARRY BEND LANDSCAPE COMPANY, a profitable commercial grounds-maintenance firm. The founder (judge), who is preparing to sell the business and retire this year, has asked you to recommend which of two contracts the company should sign and how the decision should be written and delivered.

The largest account is a hospital campus that has renewed every spring for fourteen years and comes up again next month. Its grounds are kept by the strongest crew, whose foreman is the most skilled installer and the least dependable. A regional developer that found the company through its online reviews has offered a single-season contract worth more than two years of the campus's work.

The developer needs that same crew for those same weeks. Signing the developer's contract would pull the crew off the campus during its renewal, and the campus would likely take its grounds work elsewhere. Declining the developer's contract protects the account and gives up the season's cash the founder had set aside to replace the company's aging trucks.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on which contract to sign, on what should be said to the campus and to the foreman, and on what form each message should take. The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
